references.text: The Lord relented from the disaster he had threatened to bring on his people as a result of Moses' intercession, as seen here in Numbers.
The Lord's self-revelation as a merciful and gracious God who forgives wrongdoing is the basis for him being able to say 'I have forgiven'.
The psalm describes God as a forgiving God who answered Moses and Aaron when they cried out to him.
The Lord forgives all wrongdoing, which reflects his declaration of forgiveness in Numbers 14:20.
Moses stood in the gap for the people to turn away God's wrath, and God forgave in response to his intercession.
The Lord forgives abundantly, which aligns with his declaration of forgiveness to Moses.
The Lord's promise to forgive wrongdoing and no longer remember sin, linked to the new covenant.
Micah praises God who forgives wrongdoing and passes over transgression, reflecting God's forgiving nature.
God is faithful and just to forgive sins when we confess them, a New Testament parallel to God's forgiveness.
